samples.text: For now the service runs on a manual fix: manual agency code mapping override applied to complete valuation for the period. That override is the basis for every valuation figure produced since the restart, and it stays in place until the reference data is corrected properly. The fault it covers has been confirmed as stale legacy-to-new agency code mapping in the reference data register. Because the cause sits in reference data rather than in the valuation logic, the override addresses the right layer. Legacy and cloud agency codes are not interchangeable, and the override maps them by hand for this period only. It does not repair the register, and any code that changes before the register is corrected will not be covered by it. Treat the position as provisional. It is good enough to close the period. It is not a fix, and this note will be revised when the register correction is scheduled. Teams deciding whether to wait can proceed on the current valuation for this period. The override

The valuation failed because of stale legacy-to-new agency code mapping in the reference data register. That is the confirmed cause. It replaces the first explanation logged during triage, when the cause was initially recorded as overnight ERP outage. The outage theory did not survive a look at the upstream evidence: ERP logs show no interruption during the valuation window. Once the upstream system was cleared, the review moved to the weakness behind the stale rows and classified it, for the product hierarchy sync service, as control failure: the mapping table has no registered owner and no required reviewer. Legacy and cloud agency codes are both still in use and cannot stand in for one another, so a single stale row is enough to break the lookup for every record that depends on it.
